Power or Nah

2026Personal projectSole author, published on GitHub

A pocket-sized IoT device that shows whether electricity is cheap or expensive right now. Built on an M5StickC Plus 2, it pulls Finnish spot prices directly from the ENTSO-E API, classifies them against the day's own distribution using percentile thresholds, and glows green, blue, orange or red accordingly. No app, no subscription, no friction.

Working device, running daily

The device

The challenge

Finnish electricity prices swing dramatically through the day. A price of 3 c/kWh at 2 am might be rock-bottom cheap, while the same 3 c/kWh at 6 pm could be one of the cheapest hours available. Absolute numbers are meaningless without context, and most electricity apps require unlocking a phone, opening a tab, and mentally comparing against remembered averages. The goal was a device that answers one question, is now a good time to use electricity?, at a glance from across the room.

Price levels

The classification is relative, not absolute. Percentile thresholds recalculate on every fetch from the day's own prices.

LevelFaceThreshold
Free power:Dprice below 0
Cheap:)30th percentile or below
Okay:|55th percentile or below
High:/80th percentile or below
Don't use>:[above the 95th percentile

The approach

The firmware fetches the ENTSO-E day-ahead price XML for the Finnish bidding zone (10YFI-1--------U) each minute, parses all 15-minute intervals for the current day, and sorts them to compute four percentile thresholds on the fly. The current price is classified against those thresholds rather than against a fixed table. A day where every price is high still shows CHEAP for its cheapest hours, and a day of very low prices does not mislead you into thinking 2 c/kWh is expensive.

// Dynamic thresholds, recalculated from today's sorted prices
tCheap     = percentile(todayPrices, count, 0.30);
tOkay      = percentile(todayPrices, count, 0.55);
tExpensive = percentile(todayPrices, count, 0.80);
tPain      = percentile(todayPrices, count, 0.95);

// Classify current price relative to today
if (c < 0.0)          return NEGATIVE;
if (c <= tCheap)      return CHEAP;
if (c <= tOkay)       return OKAY;
if (c <= tExpensive)  return EXPENSIVE;
return PAIN;

Key capabilities

Relative pricing
Thresholds are recalculated each fetch from the day's own prices, so cheap means cheap today rather than against a fixed baseline that goes stale as the energy market shifts.
Cheapest hour ahead
Button A shows the single cheapest upcoming price and its time window, useful when you can defer the dishwasher or an EV charge by a couple of hours.
Today's context
Button B shows the day's price range and the exact threshold values, so you can see whether today is generally cheap or expensive.
No cloud middleman
The device talks directly to the ENTSO-E public API. No third-party server, no account, no subscription, just a WiFi connection and a free API token.

Key outcomes

  • Always-on awareness. Sitting on a shelf, the device communicates price context passively. No phone, no app, no action required to stay informed.
  • Smarter consumption habits. A quick glance before running a high-load appliance is enough. Over time it shifts energy use toward off-peak hours without any planning effort.
  • End-to-end ownership. From API parsing and XML manipulation on an ESP32 to percentile maths in C++, every part of the stack was written and debugged from scratch.
